decisions.reason: The original fully visible disclosure control renders 'Show handover notes' on two lines, but its rounded left boundary visibly cuts off the beginning of the first letter of both lines. This is word/glyph clipping inside the component, not a viewport-edge fragment or a missing semantic label. Other required text is present; the explicit no-visible-word-clipping wrapping proposition is false.

The disclosure control’s rounded left boundary visibly occludes leading glyph portions in both lines of 'Show handover notes' while its native box is fully visible. The separate content blocks otherwise do not collide, but the proposition also excludes unintended occlusion. This is that occlusion, not a line-breaking complaint.

attributions.reason: Original same-state frames [24, 25] show the identical curved cuts at the two-line disclosure’s leading edge with its entire native activation box inside the viewport. The production Compose TextButton uses zero content padding and its default rounded shape; the component owns this disclosure and its typography. The clip moves with the control across scroll positions, so host viewport clipping, missing state evidence and resizing of contact sheets do not explain it. This is one disclosure-shape clipping cause manifested in both qualitative atoms, not two independent bugs.
